dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

blocks.text: [F] Hindustan Zinc (HZL) mines zinc-lead ore at captive underground mines in Rajasthan (Rampura Agucha, Sindesar Khurd, Rajpura Dariba, Zawar, Kayad; Bamnia Kalan under development), smelts it at Chanderiya, Dariba and Debari and refines silver at Pantnagar, Uttarakhand (AR2026 p.70, p.165, p.388). subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. The price already sits above every DCF scenario. [F] Price is Rs 589 against fair values of Rs 293.1 (bear), Rs 415.3 (base) and Rs 531.1 (bull); the reverse DCF implies a 21.2% 5-year sales CAGR vs 11.2% in the base case (NUMBERS).

2. Record earnings are price-led, not volume-led. [F] FY26 refined metal was 1,048 kt vs 1,052 kt, silver 627 t vs 687 t and lead 197 kt vs 225 kt (AR2026 p.322). [F] Revenue still rose 20% (NUMBERS). [AI] A silver or zinc reversal hits earnings directly.

3. Value leaks to the parent. [F] The strategic services and brand fee to Vedanta Ltd rose from 2% to 3% of consolidated turnover from 1 April 2025, taking the charge from Rs 658 cr to Rs 1,171 cr (AR2026 p.596). [F] Dividends were Rs 12,253 cr in FY25 and Rs 31,901 cr in FY23; the rating agency links payouts to debt servicing at Vedanta Resources, rated BB/Stable (RATING).

4. Regulatory and governance scrutiny. [F] The auditor's opinion carries an emphasis of matter on short-seller allegations and regulators' information requests (AR2026 p.551). [F] SEBI issued an administrative warning on 30 April 2026 on Audit Committee approvals and related-party disclosures (AR2026 p.340). [F] CRISIL notes ED searches at Vedanta group offices under FEMA (RATING).
5. Board independence is structurally deficient. [F] Only 3 of 9 directors are independent, breaching Reg. 17(1), with repeated exchange fines of about Rs 36.5 lakh a year (AR2026 p.384, p.392-395).

6. Leadership churn. [F] The CFO left on 30 May 2026 (AR2026 p.342). [F] An independent director resigned effective 30 April 2026 without a stated reason (AR2026 p.358). [F] The CEO was re-appointed for only two months before a new CEO took over on 1 August 2026 (AR2026 p.15; CALL Jul 2026).

7. Large disputed tax and royalty claims. [F] Rs 12,387 cr of 80IA/80IC tax exposure is outside the contingent-liability table (AR2026 p.525). [F] A Rs 1,925 cr royalty show-cause notice is open, and the State may recompute royalty, DMF, NMET and interest (AR2026 p.598).

8. Heavy capex ahead. [F] Rs 40,000-50,000 cr of capex over five years (AR2026 p.132) against 5-year cumulative FCF of Rs 52,748 cr (NUMBERS). [AI] The two cannot both fund today's dividend levels and full capex if prices normalise.
9. Single-state concentration. [F] All mines are in Rajasthan, and royalty per tonne of mined metal rose more than 125% in six years (RATING).

10. The overhang is persistent. [F] Promoter holding fell from 64.92% to 60.71% over 12 quarters and the Government of India's stake fell from 29.54% to 27.92% (NUMBERS). [F] 5.73% of share capital is pledged by the promoter (AR2026 p.510).

Is the margin structural? [F] Q1 FY27 margin was 59% with silver at US$73.2/oz and zinc at US$3,466/t (PPT Jul 2026). [AI] The market may be capitalising peak prices. The counter-view is that cost fell 16% YoY, which is not price-related.
Silver volumes. [F] FY26 silver fell 9% to 627 t, below the 680±10 t guidance (AR2026 p.322; CALL Oct 2025). [AI] The market may assume volume growth that has not appeared yet.

Capital allocation. [AI] If capex of Rs 40-50k cr is executed at the IRR above 18% that management claims (PPT Jul 2026 p.27), the market may be under-pricing growth. If it coincides with parent cash needs, it may be over-pricing the dividend.

Governance discount. [AI] Minorities may be over-penalising a group-level risk that has not caused a monetary penalty at HZL so far. The warning, the emphasis of matter and the FEMA searches are evidence it is not fully resolved.
Government stake sale. [AI] A disinvestment could widen free float, or it could cap the price. [MC] Management gives no update (CALL Jul 2026).

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus framing is 'low-cost silver-rich miner with a doubling plan'. Our reading is that the stock already prices more than the bull DCF (NUMBERS), while recent evidence runs the other way: volumes flat to down (AR2026 p.322), guidance misses on refined metal and silver in FY26, a sharp reduction in stated tailings output (100 kt in CALL Oct 2025 vs 30-35 kt in CALL Jul 2026), a rising brand fee, and a regulatory warning. The asset quality is not in doubt. The debate is whether minority shareholders capture the asset's economics at 10.99x book (NUMBERS) given the parent's claims on cash.

subsections.title: Critical minerals and fertiliser: narrative vs reality

blocks.text: [F] Tungsten (Balepalyam, 0.07 MnT resource), potash (18.07 MnT), and REE blocks in UP (0.182 MnT) and Karnataka are at exploration or licence stage, with mining timelines of 2030 or later (PPT Jul 2026 p.8). [F] The Gundlupet status is inconsistent: the presentation's highlights slide says 'Secured mining lease' and the call says 'securing a mining lease', but the presentation's block table says 'Declared preferred bidder, Letter of Intent awaited', and the CEO says the block is at 'G2 level' with first production maybe 2031-32 (PPT Jul 2026 p.4, p.8; CALL Jul 2026). These are not reconciled. [AI] None of this contributes revenue within the DCF horizon. Government and anchor-customer exposure is nil today.

[AI] The fertiliser plant is the only near-term diversification. It converts captive sulphuric acid into phosphoric acid and DAP, is overdue (AR2026 p.584), and is still awaiting environmental clearance for the DAP stage [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). Its economics are undisclosed.

[F] Rs 3,823 cr, 10 Mtpa feed, target Q4 FY28 (AR2026 p.31). [MC] Expected output was 'about 100 KT odd zinc metal' (CALL Oct 2025) and is now '30, 35 kt of zinc' (CALL Jul 2026). [AI] This roughly 65-70% reduction was not explained on the call. If the lower figure is right, capital intensity is about Rs 110-127 cr per kt of annual zinc [E] (3,823/35 to 3,823/30), well above the Debari smelter at about Rs 48 cr per kt [E] (12,000/250). That smelter figure includes mines.

blocks.text: [F] The reverse DCF finds that today's EV requires a constant 21.2% 5-year sales CAGR at the 51% base margin, 14.8% WACC and 5.5% terminal growth. That compares with 11.2% for the base case, 12.5% historical 5-year sales CAGR and 6.2% 3-year CAGR (NUMBERS). [F] The bull case starts at 19.9% and fades to 13%, giving Rs 531.1, still 9.8% below the price (NUMBERS).

[AI] Key forensic conclusion: at the model's margin, the price requires growth nearly double the 5-year record and above the bull case. That growth would have to come almost entirely from metal prices, since refined volume has been flat since FY23 (AR2026 p.142, p.322).

[AI] The reverse DCF holds margin at 51%. If silver and zinc prices simply stay at Q1 FY27 levels (59% margin, PPT Jul 2026), the required growth would be far lower. [AI] The model also credits no liquid investments, and the 2x expansion is not in the base. [AI] So the price may be discounting persistence of current prices plus Phase-1 volumes rather than 21% growth. That is a commodity-price bet, not a growth bet. Investors should judge it on their silver and zinc price view.

items: [AI] Upside: the DCF gives no credit for about Rs 12.9k cr of liquid investments [F] (RATING) and models a 51% margin; if silver stays elevated, cash generation is well above the base.
[AI] Downside: volume guidance credibility is weak and project outputs have been revised down, so the 2x story may deliver later and smaller than headline.

blocks.text: [AI] Good path: Debari and tailings delivered by FY29, refined capacity heading to 1.4 Mt, silver at 700-800 t, COP below US$1,000/t, governance normalised. Bad path: prices revert to FY24-like conditions (47% margin, NUMBERS) while capex peaks, dividends demanded by the parent push HZL into net debt, and regulatory matters escalate. Both paths are plausible; the current price embeds the first.

[F] At Rs 589 the stock trades above all three DCF values. Measured from the price, the bull value (Rs 531.1) is 9.8% lower, the base value (Rs 415.3) 29.5% lower and the bear value (Rs 293.1) 50.2% lower (NUMBERS). [AI] The gap is explained by the market capitalising current silver and zinc prices and Phase-1 volumes. Our model uses a through-cycle 51% margin and gives no credit for liquid investments. The asset quality is exceptional. The minority-shareholder economics and valuation are the constraints.

[AI] Horizon: this is a commodity-cycle and governance call, suited to investors with an explicit silver and zinc price view and tolerance for parent-related risk. Re-review at the Q2 FY27 results (October 2026: volumes, silver, COP, net cash after dividends); at the Q3 FY27 board decision on the ~650 kt programme; at the FY27 annual report (auditor MSKA's first opinion, RPT note, contingent liabilities); and on any SEBI, ED or demerger disclosure.

summary.one_line: Hindustan Zinc owns a first-quartile, 25-year captive zinc-lead-silver resource and is generating record cash on peak silver prices, but at Rs 589 the shares trade above even our bull DCF value (Rs 531.1), while volumes are flat, the parent's brand fee has risen to 3% of turnover, and 2026 brought a SEBI warning, an audit emphasis of matter and a full leadership turnover.
